framework: Study design for low-tick GCN conversion. A frozen residual GCN contains four node activation sites and two hidden readout sites. The continuous recovery diagnostic tests conditional sensitivity; finite-event calibration and first-site residual allocation test realizable corrections. Local, feature-only and permuted-operator controls separate residual selection from use of the actual graph mapping. No architecture shown here represents a demonstrated superior method.
ideal_sensitivity: Conditional ideal recovery at T1 on the full, historically exposed validation splits. Bars show the mean fraction of teacher-prediction disagreement closed across three teachers; error bars are sample standard deviations across teachers. Groups differ in size and their effects are nonadditive. Continuous recovery is a sensitivity diagnostic rather than a finite-event converter.
allocation_contrasts: Paired actual-graph allocation accuracy minus each control on 512 validation graphs for teacher 41. Error bars are descriptive 95 percent normal intervals over paired per-graph correctness differences. They describe graph sampling for one teacher, with no multiplicity adjustment or seed-level inference. The stronger local fit has no extra events and is an accuracy reference rather than an event-matched control. All T2 policies retain their T1-fitted offsets.
mechanism_runtime: Immediate message reconstruction and diagnostic implementation cost. Left: T1 accuracy versus normalized message MSE measured under the actual graph operator for every allocation policy; lower MSE need not yield higher accuracy. Right: synchronized host time per graph on an RTX 3060, using cached batches of 32, five warmups and 20 randomized-interleaved repeats. Boxes show quartiles and medians, whiskers extend to 1.5 interquartile ranges, and points show repeats. Measurements include policy instrumentation and exclude teacher forward and data transfer; they are software timings rather than energy measurements.
historical: Historical official-test accuracy (percent), mean and sample SD across three teacher seeds, with 10,000 test graphs per dataset. Local and graph-logit objectives fit the same 693 offsets using the same event code. These historically exposed results provide baseline context, not independent confirmation of the new candidates.
realizability: T1 validation accuracy (percent) for teacher 41 on 512 graphs. Scalars count fitted offsets or first-site amplitude values, not total model storage. Adam fits use 64 updates; the hard grid uses 33 candidates per offset, Lloyd alphabets use 16 iterations, and refined alphabets add one coordinate sweep. These different fitting budgets support diagnostic comparisons within each family, not a budget-matched ranking across families.
allocation: Fixed-opportunity residual allocation: validation accuracy (percent), teacher 41, 512 graphs. All rows share the same T1-fitted all-local offsets (learning rate 0.001). Each nonbase policy selects one quarter of nodes rounded up within each graph, with 146 possible extra scalar events per selected node. Equal opportunity does not equalize nonzero event counts. The base emits no extra corrections.
mechanism_cost: T1 normalized immediate next-message MSE and median diagnostic time. MSE is measured under the actual graph operator for all policies. Timings use identical cached batches of 32, five warmups and 20 synchronized randomized-interleaved repeats on an RTX 3060; they include instrumentation and exclude teacher forward and data transfer. See the repeat distributions in the accompanying figure.
